drivingQuestion: If fear of Heaven is God's only treasure, how can the verse present it as the small thing God asks?
outcomeNote: The difficulty is answered by locating the verse's perspective in Moses, supported by R' Ḥanina's parable of the vessel.

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: הַכֹּל בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם, חוּץ מִיִּרְאַת שָׁמַיִם. שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְעַתָּה יִשְׂרָאֵל מָה ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ שׁוֹאֵל מֵעִמָּךְ כִּי אִם לְיִרְאָה״.
segments.en: Tangentially, the Gemara cites an additional statement by Rabbi Ḥanina concerning principles of faith. «And Rabbi Ḥanina said: Everything is in the hands of Heaven, except for fear of Heaven.» Man has free will to serve God or not, «as it is stated: “And now Israel, what does the Lord your God ask of you other than to fear» the Lord your God, to walk in all of His ways, to love Him and to serve the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul” (Deuteronomy 10:12). The Lord asks man to perform these matters because ultimately, the choice is in his hands.

segments.he: אַטּוּ יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם מִילְּתָא זוּטַרְתָּא הִיא? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי: אֵין לוֹ לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּבֵית גְּנָזָיו אֶלָּא אוֹצָר שֶׁל יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״יִרְאַת ה׳ הִיא אוֹצָרוֹ״.
segments.en: The verse says: What does the Lord your God ask of you other than to fear the Lord your God. The Gemara asks: «Is fear of Heaven a minor matter» that it can be presented as if God is not asking anything significant? «Didn’t Rabbi Ḥanina say in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai: The Holy One, Blessed be He, has nothing in his treasury other than a treasure of fear of Heaven, as it is stated: “Fear of the Lord is his treasure”» (Isaiah 33:6). The Lord values and treasures fear of Heaven over all else.

segments.he: אִין, לְגַבֵּי מֹשֶׁה מִילְּתָא זוּטַרְתָּא הִיא. דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: מָשָׁל לְאָדָם שֶׁמְבַקְּשִׁים מִמֶּנּוּ כְּלִי גָּדוֹל, וְיֵשׁ לוֹ — דּוֹמֶה עָלָיו כִּכְלִי קָטָן. קָטָן, וְאֵין לוֹ — דּוֹמֶה עָלָיו כִּכְלִי גָּדוֹל.
segments.en: The Gemara responds: «Indeed, for Moses» fear of Heaven «is a minor matter. As Rabbi Ḥanina stated: It is comparable to one who is asked for a large vessel and he has» one, «it seems to him like a small vessel» because he owns it. However, one who is asked for just a «small» vessel and he does not have one, «it seems to him like a large vessel.» Therefore, Moses could say: What does the Lord your God ask of you other than to fear, because in his eyes it was a minor matter.

moves.cueHe: ואמר רבי חנינא: הכל בידי שמים, חוץ מיראת שמים
moves.summary: Chained by ואמר to R' Ḥanina's statements in the previous unit: everything is in Heaven's hands except fear of Heaven.
moves.about: the prooftext that God asks only fear of Him, showing that fear is left to man's choice

moves.cueHe: שנאמר: ועתה ישראל מה ה׳ אלהיך שואל מעמך כי אם ליראה
moves.summary: Brings the verse in which God asks only fear of Him.
moves.about: a further dictum of R' Ḥanina, chained to his statements in the preceding unit: everything is in Heaven's hands except fear of Heaven

moves.cueHe: אטו יראת שמים מילתא זוטרתא היא?
moves.summary: Objects that the verse's 'only' makes fear of Heaven trivial, which it is not.
moves.about: fear of Heaven cannot be the small thing the verse implies, since R' Ḥanina himself called it God's only treasure

moves.cueHe: והאמר רבי חנינא משום רבי שמעון בן יוחי
moves.summary: Grounds the objection in R' Ḥanina's own tradition from Rashbi that fear of Heaven is God's only treasure.
moves.about: R' Ḥanina's own dictum that God's treasury holds nothing but fear of Heaven, used against his first statement

moves.cueHe: אין, לגבי משה מילתא זוטרתא היא
moves.summary: Answers that it is indeed a small matter — for Moses, who was speaking.
moves.about: fear of Heaven is a small matter for Moses, who possessed it, even though it is great in itself

moves.cueHe: דאמר רבי חנינא: משל לאדם שמבקשים ממנו כלי גדול
moves.summary: The parable of the vessel: what you own looks small, what you lack looks large.
moves.about: R' Ḥanina's parable of the vessel — large when you have it it seems small, small when you lack it it seems large — supporting the answer
